assets.name: annotations
assets.notes: Download the public annotation export from the authors, then import the local CSV/JSON/JSONL file.

sources.notes: The paper reports 21k+ expert cue annotations for nearly 5k tracks. SAUND.AI never resolves linked commercial track audio automatically.

sources.name: UnmixDB
sources.rights_status: source description states CC-licensed redistributable dance tracks; still requires SAUND.AI production rights review

assets.name: README.txt
assets.notes: Resolved dynamically through the Zenodo record API.

sources.notes: The importer accepts an extracted UnmixDB directory and normalizes tab-separated start/end/label ground truth.

sources.name: Free Music Archive (FMA)
sources.rights_status: metadata is CC BY 4.0; each audio track keeps the artist-selected license and must be filtered/reviewed before production use
sources.notes: SAUND.AI imports metadata first and preserves per-track license fields. It does not mark the whole audio corpus production-cleared.

sources.name: ListenBrainz public listens
sources.rights_status: public listen data is published CC0; SAUND.AI still requires privacy/product review before production personalization training

assets.name: listenbrainz-listens-dump.tar.zst
assets.notes: Use an official current mirror, extract the dump, then point the importer at the extracted listens directory.

sources.notes: The normalizer hashes user identifiers and stores adjacent listening edges, not raw usernames.

sources.name: Medley2K

assets.name: annotations
assets.notes: Import the downloaded transition metadata/JSON/CSV export. MIDI/audio acquisition is intentionally not automated.

sources.notes: Used as a structural prior only; medley transitions are not treated as proof of professional DJ taste.
